storyboard.claim: Stripping the romantic myth feels unfair but is honest about how culture works.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator frowns and thinks; no icon reads 'strip the myth' literally.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the gatekeeper-stamp point: the myth of the lone genius is now being stripped away.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: staging shows reflection only; the callout carries the claim.
storyboard.staging: Host frowns and thinks: unfair, but honest.

callout.text: IF A TREE FALLS IN THE FOREST

storyboard.claim: The tree-in-the-forest puzzle is posed as a philosophical question.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tree icon standing for the falling tree of the thought experiment.
storyboard.onScreenText: IF A TREE FALLS IN THE FOREST
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the myth to a classic question about whether a thing exists without a perceiver.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the thought experiment on screen so the muted viewer knows what question is being asked.
storyboard.staging: Narrator thinks while the tree icon carries the falling-tree image.

storyboard.claim: The tree makes vibrations, but without a listener it makes no sound.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator explains; the callout splits vibration from sound.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the puzzle: yes to physics, no to sound.
storyboard.addedInformation: Separates the two meanings of 'sound' in the question.
storyboard.staging: Host explains the physics with a neutral, talking face.

callout.text: SOUND NEEDS AN EAR AND A BRAIN

storyboard.claim: Sound is a biological event that needs an ear and a brain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator thinks; no icon reads 'ear and brain' literally, so the callout carries the claim.
storyboard.onScreenText: SOUND NEEDS AN EAR AND A BRAIN
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reason the previous line says there is no sound.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names what perceives: an ear and a brain turn vibration into meaning.
storyboard.staging: Narrator thinks through the definition of sound.

storyboard.claim: Van Gogh was profoundly expressive and personally brilliant.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The painter, alone in a room, speaking warmly about the work.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concedes the point about the person before the next line introduces the field.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the painter stands in for Van Gogh (not in the bible); the warmth is genuine admiration.
storyboard.staging: The painter speaks with genuine warmth, alone at his work.

callout.text: THE FIELD FINALLY LET HIM IN

storyboard.claim: The painter's work changed the domain only after the field admitted him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door icon: the field holds the way in, and the painter stands outside it.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE FIELD FINALLY LET HIM IN
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from personal brilliance to the field's admission.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the gatekeeper as the one who opens the door.
storyboard.staging: The painter slumps in sadness while the gatekeeper stands by the door.

callout.text: CULTURAL IMPACT, NOT THE PERSONAL ACT

storyboard.claim: Creativity is measured by cultural impact, not by the personal act.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator talks; the callout names the shift from personal act to cultural impact.
storyboard.onScreenText: CULTURAL IMPACT, NOT THE PERSONAL ACT
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the point as a question back to the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the contrast explicit with 'not' on screen.
storyboard.staging: Host talks, agreeing with the impact point.

storyboard.claim: No single person declares genius; society has the final vote on shared culture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The gatekeeper at the panel table points to the verdict.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the panel image: the gatekeeper decides, not the individual.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the final vote on the panel rather than on a single genius.
storyboard.staging: The gatekeeper points to the verdict at the long panel table.

callout.text: A LOT MORE WORK THAN THAT

storyboard.claim: Creativity is not a divine spark you are born with; it takes much more work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator talks; no icon reads 'work' literally in the vocabulary, so the callout carries the claim.
storyboard.onScreenText: A LOT MORE WORK THAN THAT
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the thesis from the start of the episode.
storyboard.addedInformation: Replaces the gift myth with effort, stated on screen.
storyboard.staging: Host talks firmly, rejecting the gift idea.

storyboard.claim: A personal spark needs the domain's kindling and the field's oxygen to catch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fire icon: the spark needs fuel to burn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the circuit as a fire that needs fuel.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fire icon makes the kindling metaphor literal; the callout names the fuel.
storyboard.staging: Narrator thinks while the fire icon burns.

storyboard.claim: Gatekeeper friction does not make creativity less; it makes it more mysterious.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator thinks; the callout states the reversal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the friction point: the field does not diminish creativity.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the reversal on screen so the muted viewer does not read 'less'.
storyboard.staging: Host thinks, reaching a reversed conclusion.

storyboard.claim: A great idea is a rare moment when person, culture and gatekeepers align.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator talks warmly; the callout lists the three forces.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the thesis: the three parts align.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the three forces on screen so the system is visible without sound.
storyboard.staging: Host talks with warm wonder about the rare alignment.

storyboard.claim: Ask which part of the system is holding you back.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains read as being held back; the host points at the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the system idea to the viewer's own life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains make 'holding back' literal; the point makes it personal.
storyboard.staging: Host points at the audience while the chains icon shows restraint.

storyboard.claim: Are you missing the deep knowledge of your domain, or hiding your work from judgment?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A book icon: deep domain knowledge; the host thinks in a library.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First of two self-check questions; the second (hiding work) is in the same narration.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book icon makes the knowledge literal.
storyboard.staging: Host thinks, worried, beside the book icon in a library.

storyboard.claim: Waiting around for a magical spark is the wrong approach; the spark must be built.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lightbulb icon: the idea everyone waits for; the host sits idle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the self-check: the alternative to building is waiting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Blank apathy on the host sets up the rejection of passive waiting.
storyboard.staging: Host sits with a blank face while the lightbulb shows the idea everyone waits for.
